expectations.text: Selects the right objectives: prototype-related labels (Proto Vehicles / Test Vehicles — and Proto Parts / Proto Events where relevant to the activity) rather than only the confidentiality labels
expectations.evidence: Table lists Proto Parts, Proto Vehicles, Test Vehicles, and Proto Events; response states "Test Vehicles is the most directly applicable label, and Proto Vehicles may also apply" and treats a confidentiality label (Confidential/Strictly Confidential) as a separate, additional determination rather than the primary answer.

expectations.text: States the level rule correctly: physical prototype labels require AL3 — a comprehensive ON-SITE assessment including physical inspection
expectations.evidence: "All of the physical prototype labels (Proto Parts, Proto Vehicles, Test Vehicles, Proto Events) require AL3 — a comprehensive on-site assessment involving evidence review, interviews, and physical inspection of your facilities/processes."

expectations.text: Describes the Prototype Protection catalogue accurately: a dedicated ISA 6 module (22 controls) covering physical/organizational protections — perimeter and zone security, camouflage and transport rules, test-drive protections, photo/film controls, personnel commitments
expectations.evidence: "The Prototype Protection catalogue (22 controls under ISA 6; restructuring to 20 controls in 2 domains under ISA2027) covers physical and organizational protection measures including: Perimeter and zone security ... Camouflage and transport rules ... Test-drive protections ... Film/photo controls ... Personnel commitments"

expectations.text: Notes the ISA2027 change accurately where versioning comes up: the prototype module is restructured (20 controls in 2 domains, new PTS label structure) for assessments ordered from January 1, 2027
expectations.evidence: "ISA2027 was published July 1, 2026, and becomes mandatory for assessments ordered from January 1, 2027 — notably, it restructures the prototype module from 22 to 20 controls across 2 domains and introduces a new PTS prototype-label structure."

expectations.text: Covers the practical path: ENX registration and scoping of the testing locations, ENX-accredited provider with prototype competence, evidence and site readiness for physical inspection, maturity-3 target with cutback
expectations.evidence: Practical next steps cover maturity-3/cutback fully ("targeting maturity 3 on all applicable requirements (cutback rules mean weak spots in either catalogue will drag your result down...)") and site readiness partially ("Plan for AL3: budget for an on-site visit"), but never mention ENX portal registration or scoping the testing locations as a step, and never call for selecting a provider with specific prototype-assessment competence (the only mention of an 'ENX-accredited audit provider' is a generic line in the closing disclaimer, not part of the practical path).
